findings.title: getClientsWithPermission likely returns the type name instead of client IDs
findings.body: `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` matches resources whose `type` is "Clients". Per-client resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` through `resourceStore.create(server, name, owner)`, and no type is set on them. So the search probably returns only the "all clients" resource, and the code adds `resource.getName()` ("Clients"). The method therefore returns "Clients" instead of client IDs. That makes it useless for filtering clients by granted scope and gives wrong results to any caller. It also has no test coverage.

findings.title: Possible NPE when the Clients type resource is not found
findings.body: `getResourceTypeResource` returns null if the schema isn't supported for the server, or if no "Clients" resource exists. For example, the "all-clients" resource can be missing in a realm whose admin-permissions client was initialised before CLIENTS was added to the schema. The result is passed straight to `findByResource(server, resource)` and then to `resource.getScopes()`. A null result throws a NullPointerException (an HTTP 500) instead of returning false (deny). There is no null check.

findings.title: getResourceName not extended for the Clients resource type
findings.body: `getResourceName` handles only `USERS` and resolves the user's username. For permissions of type `Clients` it falls through to `resource.getDisplayName()`. Per-client resources are named by client UUID and have no display name, so the name is null or the raw ID. "All clients" is not mapped to a friendly name either. Resource names shown for client permissions are therefore wrong, and the Clients type is only half-integrated in the schema.

findings.title: ClientRemovedEvent still calls V1-only setPermissionsEnabled, which throws in V2
findings.body: The listener now runs only when V1 `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled. `management()` still returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever V2 is enabled, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. If both features are enabled, deleting a client throws from the removal event listener. The gate hides the problem only when V1 is disabled. The listener should skip V2 explicitly or tolerate the unsupported call. Gating on V1 also silently changes the cleanup behavior of existing listeners.

findings.title: Tests mutate the admin client's own secret and shared client state without cleanup
findings.body: `testConfigureOnlyOneClient` calls `generateNewSecret()` on `myclient`, which is the client `realmAdminClient` authenticates with (the secret is "mysecret"). Token re-acquisition for later calls, or in later tests that share the realm, can then fail with 401. `testManageOnlyOneClient` renames `myclient` and removes a default client scope. `testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` creates client roles and composites. `onAfter` removes only permissions, so this state leaks into other tests and can make them order-dependent or flaky.

findings.title: JUnit 4 Assert.fail used in a JUnit 5 test
findings.body: The test imports `org.junit.Assert.fail` (JUnit 4) while the rest of the class and the sibling tests use `org.junit.jupiter.api`. This relies on a transitive JUnit 4 dependency and is inconsistent with the other tests, which use `org.junit.jupiter.api.Assertions.fail`.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods says 'Returns'
findings.body: `requireView()` and `requireViewClientScopes()` are void methods that throw ForbiddenException. Their new Javadoc says "Returns {@code true} if ...". The wording is wrong and contradicts the other `require*` docs, which say "Throws ForbiddenException".

findings.title: Dead code and unused imports
findings.body: The private `getEvaluationContext` method is never used. The `logger` field is also unused, as are the imports `Scope`, `TOKEN_EXCHANGE`, `ClientModelIdentity`, `DefaultEvaluationContext` and `EvaluationContext`. This looks copy-pasted from V1 and should be removed.
